questions.stem: A service moves an image-resizing job that does pure computation, and never waits on I/O, from a fixed pool sized to the cores onto virtual threads. Per this page, what does the move gain?

options.text: Nothing, since the job has no point at which its thread can unmount
options.says: The page says virtual threads help only when tasks spend their time waiting; CPU-bound work gives them nothing to unmount at, so a pool sized to the cores stays the right tool.

options.text: Shorter jobs, since a virtual thread runs code faster than a platform one
options.says: The page says virtual threads do not make a single task run faster; the same computation takes the same time on either kind of thread.

options.text: More jobs per second, since many more threads can now share the cores
options.says: The page ties the throughput gain to tasks that wait; when every job keeps a core busy, more threads only queue for the same cores.

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens to the carrier thread while a virtual thread it was running waits in Thread.sleep()?

options.text: It stays tied to that virtual thread until the sleep is over
options.says: The page describes this for a platform thread; a virtual thread is mounted only while it runs and detaches from its carrier at a blocking call.

options.text: It is free to run other virtual threads in the meantime
options.says: The page says the sleeping virtual thread is unmounted, so its carrier picks up other virtual threads, and the sleeper later resumes on any free carrier.

options.text: It is handed back to the OS and a new one is made later
options.says: The page says carriers are platform threads kept in a dedicated ForkJoinPool and reused; nothing is handed back to the OS.
